text.p: Jose Maria Olazabal began his comeback from 18 months of injury with a remarkable three-under-par 69 in the first round of the Desert Classic on Thursday.
Three birdies in the last four holes of the 7,102-yard Emirates Course lifted the 31-year-old Spaniard into a strong position to achieve his first objective of making the halfway cut.
Olazabal, the 1994 Masters champion, has been plagued with foot problems that threatened to consign him to a wheelchair for life until a German doctor put him on the road to recovery.
"Obviously I'm pleased but I have to say I wasn't as fully concentrated in the same way I would have been if what I've been through didn't happen," Olazabal said.
His 69 left him four shots behind joint first round leaders Colin Montgomerie, the European number one and defending champion, and Spaniard Domingo Hospital. They carded 65s.
"I didn't put any score in my mind. What I said to myself was just try my best and try to hit as many good shots as I can and don't get angry with bad shots," said Olazabal.
"I loved the competition and that's what I practise for. That's the thing I missed the most.
"But I don't want to talk about my feet. I will tell you how I feel at the end of the week."
Olazabal's three late birdies resulted from putts of 30 and 18 feet at the 15th and 16th and a 90-yard pitch to three feet at the long 18th.
Montgomerie played in a red-hot three-ball with Bernhard Langer and Irishman Padraig Harrington, who both carded 66.
Montgomerie won this event last year with a stroke voted the "shot of the year" on the European Tour, a driver from the fairway across a lake to set up a birdie four on the final green.
On Thursday he hit a shot that was even better to set up an eagle three at the 550-yard 13th.
He pulled his drive left into a sandy lie and, with a sprawling bunker guarding the approach to the green, it seemed he had no choice but to play short.
But he hit a two iron 255 yards, landing over the bunker on the front of the green and rolling up the slope for an easy tap-in from two feet.
"It was an uphill lie with the ball above my feet and I had to make sure I didn't topple over or the shot might have finished in the lake beside the green," he said.
Hospital, who finished 37th on the European money list last year, had seven birdies and did not drop a shot.
Afterwards he spoke for the Spanish players about Olazabal's comeback.
"We thought he had no chance of coming back. People were saying he had no chance of walking again," Hospital said.
"Of course, we're really happy for him. We thought he would finish in a wheelchair.
"I used to phone him once or twice a month. He tried to sound optimistic, saying he felt much better, but you felt it was just words.
"The pain was unbelievable for him just to stand. When you saw that, you thought he had no chance."
Langer, now using a broomhandle putter, made seven birdies on the first 13 holes and another at the last but dropped shots at the 16th and 17th.
Harrington, a close contender for rookie of the year honours last year, was not overawed by the company he was in and birdied five successive holes on the back nine.
"It can go two ways when you are drawn with two fabulous players. You can play badly and be crushed but fortunately they lifted me," he said.
World number one Greg Norman carded a 71 and Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros continued his poor run by dropping three shots on the last two holes for a 74.
Fog delayed the start of play and nine players from the 131-man field must complete their opening rounds on Friday.
